overview: This Senate resolution designates May 2025 as 'ALS Awareness Month.' ALS, or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (also called Lou Gehrig's disease), is a disease that gradually destroys the nerve cells controlling muscles, leading to paralysis, and most people live only two to five years after diagnosis. The resolution notes that there is no cure, that the cause is unknown in most cases, and that military veterans are more likely to be diagnosed. It commits the Senate to improving access to treatment and support, finding causes, and easing the burden on patients, and it thanks families, caregivers, researchers, and volunteers. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on June 5, 2025.
for: Supporters say raising awareness of ALS helps patients and families and supports the push for research and earlier access to treatment.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or provide funding for ALS research or care.
